title: 💸 Musk warns: the AI industry could run out of money in 2027! Hundreds of billions in working capital!
body: 💸 Musk warns: the AI industry could run out of money in 2027! Hundreds of billions in working capital!
On November 21, Elon Musk warned that the AI industry could face a severe liquidity crisis in 2027, in a conversation on the 'X' platform with AI researcher François Chollet.

Musk sees the problem not as weak demand, but as timing: companies pay for graphics cards, build data centers and secure energy before any customer pays for a single query, and a delay of a few months in turning this computing into revenue could require hundreds of billions of additional dollars in working capital.

Musk said 'the liquidity crunch will be insane next year', adding that a cumulative delay of a few months between paying for computing and making it reliable enough to generate revenue means hundreds of billions of additional dollars just for working capital.
He pointed out that debt markets have largely closed their doors to new cloud computing providers that rely on renting out AI power, if they do not have meaningful revenue outside AI data centers.

Musk also predicted a wave of mergers or outright failures among more than 200 companies in the AI data center field, amid weak investor confidence and tightening credit conditions, while he himself aims to add more than 10 gigawatts of new computing capacity in 2027.

The warnings come as 'Goldman Sachs' data revealed AI-related debt issuance of about $600 billion since the start of the year, with capital spending on AI approaching one trillion dollars in 2026, while 'SpaceX' closed debt financing of about $40 billion in October to buy graphics cards expected to be deployed in early 2027.
Simply put: the industry buys computing today and gets paid for it tomorrow, and if tomorrow is a few months late it needs hundreds of billions... will everyone survive the 2027 crisis?
Do you think the AI boom will continue despite the funding crisis, or is a wave of bankruptcies coming?
